required_capabilities.b_rep_ingest: Import STEP or equivalent boundary-representation solids
required_capabilities.cutter_sweep: Execute a defined cutter geometry along a prescribed path
required_capabilities.removal_volume: Compute removed or remaining material volume from the sweep
required_capabilities.gouge_judgement: Judge excess removal against a target region and tolerance
required_capabilities.operation_attribution: Attribute a violation to an individual operation id
required_capabilities.deterministic_replay: Replay the same program with a reproducible outcome

decision_rule: A backend is eligible only if all required capabilities are supported.

candidates.name: Genesis World

b_rep_ingest.evidence: Asset parsers listed: URDF, MJCF, OBJ, GLB, USD; no STEP or B-rep parser.

cutter_sweep.evidence: Physics covers rigid, FEM, MPM, particle, uipc and SAP; no CNC cutter-sweep primitive.

removal_volume.evidence: State is positions/deformations/concentrations, not a subtractive solid; the MPM 'cut dragon' example cuts deformable material, not stock removal.

gouge_judgement.evidence: No target-region or overcut predicate exists, so no reward or label for 'material that should have survived' can be defined.

operation_attribution.evidence: No operation-graph concept in the simulation interface.

deterministic_replay.evidence: GPU simulation is seedable in principle, but no machining-program replay interface is published.

candidates.training_readiness: Not trainable for this task: reinforcement learning requires a scalar reward for removed volume or gouge depth, and neither quantity is represented in the simulator state. Building them would be a new research project, not an integration step.

candidates.name: SolidCraft (SolidCore)

b_rep_ingest.evidence: Imports/exports STEP and mesh; SolidCore is a Rust port of NVIDIA SMLib.

cutter_sweep.evidence: Feature timeline is sketch/extrude/revolve/fillet; no milling operation or cutter motion.

removal_volume.evidence: Oracle checks volume, area, centre of mass and bounding box of modelled parts, not a subtractive machining result.

gouge_judgement.evidence: No masked region, tolerance band or overcut predicate.

operation_attribution.evidence: Editable feature history exists, but for modelling features, not machining operations.

deterministic_replay.evidence: Parametric rebuild is deterministic; no NC-program replay is defined.

candidates.training_readiness: Not trainable for this task: it is a modeller, not a machining environment; it offers no state transition driven by a toolpath.

candidates.name: Z-dexel + OpenCAMLib + CAMotics (current chain)

b_rep_ingest.evidence: STEP read via FreeCAD and triangulation exported to STL for finite-cutter oracle.

cutter_sweep.evidence: OpenCAMLib CylCutter dropCutter over sampled tool-centre positions.

removal_volume.evidence: Z-dexel removal simulation plus CAMotics remaining-volume cross-check (1.15% mean relative difference).

gouge_judgement.evidence: Dual-line acceptance and finite-cutter overcut depth against a 0.5 mm line; verifier blind spot quantified over 130 external parts.

operation_attribution.evidence: Structured E_GOUGE errors carry operation ids back to the planner.

deterministic_replay.evidence: Grid-based replay from stored G-code; figures and reports regenerated by scripts/reproduce.sh.

candidates.training_readiness: Not a learning environment either. It is a verifier: the contribution is an auditable acceptance protocol, not a trained policy.

conclusion: General-purpose robotics simulation and parametric CAD do not satisfy the material-removal verification contract. This is a scope boundary, not a claim that either platform is defective at its intended task.
